body:
### Summary

Downstream in Fedora, we build Rust with a custom profile called `rpm`, which inherits from `release`. For practical technical reasons, we build tests the same way.

We find that the test `git_version_info_expected` now fails to compile because

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/a1b84bcbda122236faae8fa5fdcbe16cfb76cde2/crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs#L2162

accesses the `PROFILE` environment variable at compile time, but it is not set.

```
error: environment variable `PROFILE` not defined at compile time
    --> crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs:2158:8
     |
2158 |     if env!("PROFILE") != "release" && option_env!("UV_INTERNAL__BUILD_GIT_INFO") != Some("1") {
     |        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
     |
     = help: `PROFILE` may not be available for the current Cargo target
     = help: Cargo sets build script variables at run time. Use `std::env::var("PROFILE")` instead
```

Looking at https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-build-scripts, I see:

> `PROFILE` — `release` for release builds, `debug` for other builds. This is determined based on if the profile inherits from the `dev` or `release` profile. Using this environment variable is not recommended. Using other environment variables like `OPT_LEVEL` provide a more correct view of the actual settings being used.

but I also note that this documentation section is entitled “environment variables Cargo sets for build scripts,” and that this is not a build script. The section “environment variables Cargo sets for cargo test” promises only to set `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>`, so there appear to be no documented guarantees about `PROFILE` here.

I thought of suggesting something like this,

```diff
From 076a0a55e41e217ef9b6c2b25a7c09d426e51f06 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Benjamin A. Beasley" <code@musicinmybrain.net>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 17:14:18 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] In test `git_version_info_expected`, support `PROFILE` unset

Allow this test to build in situations where the `PROFILE` environment
variable is not set, e.g. downstream in Fedora using the custom `rpm`
profile.
---
 crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs b/crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs
index e5b3ec7bd..70977f753 100644
--- a/crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs
+++ b/crates/uv/tests/it/version.rs
@@ -2155,7 +2155,9 @@ fn version_get_fallback_unmanaged_short() -> Result<()> {
 
 /// Whether this build should include Git metadata in its version output.
 fn git_version_info_expected() -> bool {
-    if env!("PROFILE") != "release" && option_env!("UV_INTERNAL__BUILD_GIT_INFO") != Some("1") {
+    if option_env!("PROFILE") != Some("release")
+        && option_env!("UV_INTERNAL__BUILD_GIT_INFO") != Some("1")
+    {
         return false;
     }
 
-- 
2.55.0

```

and that would make the test work in practice, but it’s not necessarily logically correct: `option_env!("PROFILE") != Some("release")` evaluates false even though our profile inherits from `release`.

For now, I’m just going to carry a patch that disables compiling this test via `#[cfg(false)]`, but I would be happy in principle to offer a PR that meant I didn’t have to do that forever. I’m not sure that the premise of checking `PROFILE` here is really valid, but I’m not quite sure what to suggest instead.

### Platform

Fedora Rawhide, x86_64

### Version

uv 0.12.7 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.15.0rc2
title: Test `git_version_info_expected` doesn’t compile with custom profile: `PROFILE` is unset
